class View:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rows = []
        self.notes = {}
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        self.seq = 0
        self._current_id = None

    def begin(self, query):
        self.seq += 1
        self._current_id = self.seq
        self.loading = False
        self.error = None
        return self.seq

    def finish(self, request_id, rows):
        # only the latest begun request can update rows, once
        if request_id != self._current_id:
            return False
        # older or duplicate replies return False
        # once finished, do not allow further updates
        self.rows = rows
        self._current_id = None
        return True

    def copy_rows(self):
        # copy accepted rows (deep copy?)
        # rows is list; copy shallow copy
        return self.rows.copy()

    def get_loading(self):
        return self.loading

    # notes preserved through all requests
    # no method needed; just store notes

from view import View

def test_basic():
    v = View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    assert v.get_loading() == False
    # finish with same id should succeed
    res = v.finish(id1, ['r1'])
    assert res == True
    assert v.rows == ['r1']
    # second begin
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    # finish id1 (stale) should fail
    res = v.finish(id1, ['r1b'])
    assert res == False
    # finish id2 should succeed
    res = v.finish(id2, ['r2'])
    assert res == True
    assert v.rows == ['r2']
    # begin again
    id3 = v.begin('q3')
    # finish id2 (stale) should fail
    res = v.finish(id2, ['r2b'])
    assert res == False
    # finish id3 should succeed
    res = v.finish(id3, ['r3'])
    assert res == True
    assert v.rows == ['r3']
    # copy rows
    cp = v.copy_rows()
    assert cp == ['r3']
    # notes preservation
    v.notes['job1'] = 'note1'
    # begin/finish should not clear notes
    id4 = v.begin('q4')
    res = v.finish(id4, ['r4'])
    assert res == True
    assert v.notes['job1'] == 'note1'
    # loading cleared on begin
    v.loading = True
    v.error = 'old'
    id5 = v.begin('q5')
    assert v.loading == False
    assert v.error is None
    # finish duplicate id (same seq?) should fail
    res = v.finish(id5, ['r5b'])
    assert res == False  # already finished
    # but begin again and finish same id? actually begin returns new seq, so duplicate id from earlier cannot finish
    # test that only latest begun can update rows, once
    # after finish, begin new and finish new works
    id6 = v.begin('q6')
    res = v.finish(id6, ['r6'])
    assert res == True
    assert v.rows == ['r6']

def test_duplicate_id():
    v = View()
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    v.finish(id1, ['r1'])
    # try finish id1 again should fail
    res = v.finish(id1, ['r1b'])
    assert res == False

def test_notes_preserve():
    v = View()
    v.notes['a'] = 1
    id1 = v.begin('q1')
    v.finish(id1, ['r1'])
    assert v.notes['a'] == 1
    # after another begin/finish
    id2 = v.begin('q2')
    v.finish(id2, ['r2'])
    assert v.notes['a'] == 1

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_basic()
    test_duplicate_id()
    test_notes_preserve()
    print('All tests passed')
